# Kition kit rules (read first)

<!-- kition-quality:begin (generated by kition-sdk tools/sync-quality.mjs; edit the template there) -->
## Quality rules (read first)

- Tests are the spec. Read `docs/quality.md` and the feature catalogue (`features.yaml`)
  before changing behaviour. When code and a case disagree, the case wins unless a maintainer
  approves changing the case.
- Before you finish any task, run `cargo xtask ci`. If it fails, the task is not done. Claude Code
  runs it for you through the Stop hook; agents without hooks (Codex) run it by hand and
  report the real exit code.
- Never edit expected results to make a test pass: files under `cases/**/expected/`, paths
  listed under `protected` in `features.yaml`, and the `expected`, `tolerance`, `reference`,
  `input` and `steps` of an existing `case.yaml`. If you believe an expected result is wrong,
  stop and explain why in the task's findings; only a maintainer approves expected-result changes.
- Never weaken a test to make it pass: no deleted or loosened assertions, no added
  `#[ignore]`, `.skip`, `.only` or `.todo`, no raised tolerances. kition-sdk's
  `tools/check-expected.mjs` lists every such change for the maintainers.
- Every bug fix starts with a failing case under `cases/regressions/issue-<n>/`, then the fix.
- Every new feature adds an entry to `features.yaml` and at least one gate case.
- Put the task id and the case ids in the commit message.
- Stage only your own files: `git add` them by name; never `git commit -a` or `git add -A`.
  Other sessions may have uncommitted work in the same checkout.
- Work on `kition-slide` only in its main checkout; never change, build, or commit in its worktrees (`kition-slide-wt/*`, `kition-*-wt`, `kition-naming-work`).
- Never start `cargo xtask eval` (the real-model `layer: eval` cases): only a maintainer starts it (F-QA-16). Write eval cases and check them with `--dry-run`, which calls no model.
- No compatibility layers: no aliases, old names, old file suffixes, migrations, or readers for
  old formats. Delete a replaced path in the same change.
<!-- kition-quality:end -->

This repository is Kition's `kit.doc` kit. These rules come first; the upstream rules below
still apply to the engine.

- The kit draws **its own editor**: `web/` is a React app on `@kition/kit-editor` (kition-sdk's
  shared kit UI library) with Kition Doc's ribbon, the page canvas, find and replace, and a status
  bar; a host (Kition, or `web/dev.html` for development) shows it in an iframe and talks to it
  over the Kit UI protocol (`kition-kit-ui/1`, kition-sdk `docs/platform/reference/ui-protocol.md`). Style it only
  with the host's theme tokens and kit-editor components; ribbon labels and command titles are
  Kition Doc's English text, translated by the upstream editor's `web/src/i18n/upstream/*.tsv`
  catalogs, and the editor's other strings live in `web/src/strings.ts` (`en-US`, `zh-CN`); take
  typed text through kit-editor's `TextSink` so input methods work. Files go only through the host.
- `bindings/wasm` compiles the engine to WebAssembly on the public
  `KitionAI/kition-sdk` crate; the editor runs it in a Web Worker. The contract and the Kition platform rules live in kition-sdk
  (`docs/platform/kits/engine.md`, `docs/platform/reference/ui-protocol.md`), the agent protocol
  in KHP (`github.com/kitharness/khp`);
  change them there, never here. `kition-doc-kit` must keep passing `kition_kit::testing::check_contract`,
  and `kit.json` must pass kition-sdk's `tools/check-manifest.mjs`.
- Tools run in the engine (`KitTools`): clicks, drags, typing, and keys run Kition Doc's own commands (`caret.set`, `text.insert`, the registry's shortcuts), and the caret and selection return as engine overlays. Never draw editor chrome into the rendered pixels.
- Licensed under Apache-2.0 only ([LICENSE](LICENSE)); third-party notices are listed in `NOTICE`.
  Upstream is credited only in `NOTICE`; never write upstream names anywhere else.
- Drawing objects (shapes and text boxes) share their preset outlines, `KitDrawing 1.0` commands
  (`drawing.*`), gestures and ribbon controls with the other Office kits through kition-sdk's
  `kition-office-core` crate and kit-editor's drawing controls; depend on them (from the sibling
  `../kition-sdk` checkout until the SDK publishes the crate), never copy them.
- Whatever else doc, sheet and slide all hold (equations, smart graphics, charts, ink, and
  later the PDF and picture export) belongs in `kition-office-core` too: move it there rather
  than keeping a kit's own copy.

# Kition Doc — instructions for agents

Kition Doc is the Word engine behind Kition's `kit.doc` kit: a clean-room, open-source,
Rust-native word-processing engine, compiled to WebAssembly for Kition's in-page editor and served
headless (`bindings/headless`) for Kition's agent. Siblings with the same conventions: `../kition-cad`
(2D drafting), `../kition-slide` (presentation), `../kition-sheet` (spreadsheet), `../kition-layout`
(page layout), `../kition-pdf` (PDF), `../kition-motion` (motion graphics), `../kition-film` (video
editing), `../kition-photo` (layered image editing), `../kition-vector` (vector illustration). See
`docs/kits.md` in the Kition repository and kition-sdk's `docs/platform/` for the shared conventions.

## Start every session here
1. Read `plan/STATUS.md` (current milestone, next task), then the task in `plan/execution-plan.md` and the relevant `docs/architecture.md` section. `plan/` is gitignored (local only); if it's missing, start from `docs/architecture.md`.
2. Follow the autonomous operation protocol (`plan/execution-plan.md` §5). Don't stop to ask unless a decision is genuinely the maintainers' (licensing, publishing, pushing to new remotes, secrets).

## Never crash
People trust Kition Doc with their writing; a crash loses their work. **This outranks feature work**: never ship a feature through a panic path, and fix a crash before building on top of it.
- **No panics in non-test code:** no `unwrap()`, `expect()`, `panic!`, `unreachable!`, `todo!`, `unimplemented!`; no `unsafe` (`unsafe_code = "forbid"`).
- **Errors are `Result<T, E>`** through the crate's error type and `?`. An unfinished feature returns an error or is disabled; it never panics.
- **Input-derived numbers are hostile** (files, commands, agent params): `get()` instead of `[i]`, slice strings only at char boundaries, checked/saturating arithmetic, clamp sizes, cap allocations, bound recursion.
- **Last-resort guard:** `Session::run` turns an escaped panic into an error and restores the document. It's a safety net, not a license.
- **Prove it:** every crash fix lands with a regression test. `crates/engine/engine/src/tests.rs::hostile_params_never_panic` runs every command with junk params — keep it green.
- Production crate roots carry `#![deny(clippy::unwrap_used, clippy::expect_used, clippy::panic, clippy::unimplemented, clippy::todo, clippy::unreachable)]`; new crates start with it. Tests may `unwrap` (`.clippy.toml`).

## Assets: absolutely no Microsoft (or Adobe/Avid/Autodesk) iconography or images
**This rule is non-negotiable.** Breaking it is the worst mistake you can make in this repo.
- Never copy, trace, screenshot-crop or recreate icons, images, templates, themes, clip art, fonts, cursors, sounds or any other asset from Microsoft Word/Office or any Microsoft, Adobe, Avid or Autodesk product. Not even "temporarily".
- Every asset must be **original** (drawn in code, where practical), **public domain / CC0**, **OSI open source**, or **Creative Commons that allows redistribution**, or licensed open source by a contributor who made it.
- **Every asset file has a row in [`docs/attribution.md`](docs/attribution.md)** (author, source, license). `cargo xtask assets` (part of `cargo xtask ci`) fails otherwise. Add the row in the same commit as the file.
- Fonts: new font files go to [`KitionAI/kition-fonts`](https://github.com/KitionAI/kition-fonts), never this repo; it's an optional build input (`KITION_FONTS_DIR`). Documents asking for proprietary fonts (Calibri, Aptos, Cambria…) are rendered with installed system fonts or metric-compatible open substitutes (`crates/support/fonts/src/word.rs`) — never bundle proprietary fonts.
- Templates, sample documents and themes are our own text and colours (`crates/engine/engine/src/sample.rs`, `cmd/design.rs`). Demo images are public domain, with sources recorded.

## Clean room
- Microsoft Word is installed on the dev machine and may be **observed** black-box: run it, use its UI with synthetic documents, take screenshots **of its window only** (by window id — the machine runs other work; never capture the whole desktop) stored only under `plan/word/screenshots/` (gitignored, never committed).
- Never read, disassemble or copy anything inside the Word bundle (file names/listings only). Never commit files produced by Word. Never copy Microsoft wording beyond feature names.
- File formats come from public specs: ECMA-376 / ISO 29500 (OOXML), the published RTF spec, OASIS ODF 1.3. Never copy GPL/LGPL/AGPL code (LibreOffice, AbiWord, pandoc…).

## Architecture (see `docs/architecture.md`)
| Layer | Crate | Job |
|---|---|---|
| L0 | `geom` | units, rects, measurement parsing |
| L1 | `doc`, `fonts` | document model + edit primitives; font DB, shaping, Word font substitution |
| L2 | `layout`, `docx`, `formats` | line breaking, pagination, tables, headers/footers, hit testing; OOXML I/O; TXT/MD/HTML/RTF/ODT |
| L3 | `render`, `pdf`, `proof` | vello_cpu rasteriser; krilla PDF; proofing |
| L4 | `engine` | Session, undo, **command registry**, Word feature catalog, samples, I/O dispatch |
| L5 | `kition-doc-kit` | the `KitDocument`/`KitTools` contract for Kition's in-page editor, compiled to WebAssembly |
| apps | `bindings/headless` | the headless kit executable for Kition's agent |

- **Everything is a command.** User-visible behaviour = a `CommandSpec` in `crates/engine/engine/src/cmd/*.rs` (id, label, ribbon location, shortcut, params doc, `enabled`, `run`) + tests. The web editor's ribbon, `kition-doc-kit`'s `KitTools`, and Kition's agent all dispatch by id. Programmatic calls never open dialogs.
- **Parity is measured:** `crates/engine/engine/src/catalog.rs` lists Word's ribbon/menu features with command ids. `cargo xtask parity` writes `docs/parity/parity-checklist.md`; a test enforces a floor that only rises. Implement missing ids to raise it.
- **Layering** is enforced by `cargo xtask layers`.
- **Rust only in the engine** (no handwritten JS/TS below `kition-doc-kit`). The kit's own editor, `web/`, is a React/TypeScript app by design (Kition platform `docs/platform/kits/ui.md`); **never break wasm** (`cargo xtask wasm`).

## Quality gates
Before every commit: `cargo xtask ci` (fmt, clippy -D warnings, tests, assets, layers, wasm). Commit after every arc of work that builds.

## Typing behaves like Word
Typing, Enter, Backspace, Tab, lists, AutoCorrect and AutoFormat follow Word's observed behaviour in [`docs/parity/typing-parity.md`](docs/parity/typing-parity.md), pinned by `crates/engine/engine/src/tests_typing.rs` (keys go through the same commands as the keyboard). Change behaviour, doc and tests together; a typing fix lands with a test there. Compare headlessly (drive the engine directly through tests, or `bindings/headless` over the Kit Protocol); don't drive GUIs with keystrokes on the shared machine.

## Building and running the kit
- Engine: `cargo build --release -p kition-doc` (the headless kit executable for Kition's agent).
- Editor: `cd web && pnpm install && pnpm engine && pnpm dev` (serves `dev.html`, a development host); `pnpm test:flow` runs its Playwright flow tests.
- Shell gotcha: `mv`/`cp` may be aliased interactive — use `/bin/mv -f` / `/bin/cp -f`.
- Parallel agents: separate `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` per agent; edit only the crates you own; delete your target dir when done (disk).

## Roadmap
Engine fidelity against Microsoft Word is tracked in `docs/parity/file-format-parity.md`,
`docs/parity/layout-parity.md`, `docs/parity/typing-parity.md` and the generated `docs/parity/parity-checklist.md`.
When work lands, update the relevant parity doc and bump its status line and revision history.
